title: CVE-2026-126714: phpAfterShell PHP Session Flaw Can Lead to Remote Code Execution
content_md: The PHP development team has released security updates addressing CVE-2026-126714, a critical vulnerability dubbed phpAfterShell that can turn partially overwritten session files into an arbitrary deserialization primitive and potentially remote code execution. The flaw carries a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2, Critical and affects PHP applications using the default file-based session handler. Unlike a vulnerability confined to one CMS or framework, phpAfterShell exists in PHP itself. Applications built with WordPress, Laravel, custom PHP frameworks, or other software can therefore fall within the exposure scope if they run a vulnerable PHP release and store sessions as files. Applications using Redis, databases, or other non-file session handlers are outside this specific defect. The vulnerability stems from how PHP updates existing session files. If an update is interrupted at the right moment, part of the new session data can overwrite the beginning of the file while bytes from the previous session remain at the end. PHP may later interpret this hybrid file as valid session state and deserialize attacker-controlled objects when the application calls session_start(). Successful exploitation requires several conditions, including attacker influence over session data, an interruption at a useful point during the write, and a suitable deserialization path.
